verification.note: Primary Smith opening read on the LSE resource page; Gellner’s reply at https://www.lse.ac.uk/researchAndExpertise/units/gellner/Warwick2.html consulted for cultural continuity and modern mobility/literate culture. The linked introduction dates the event to 1995, distinct from publication. Smith credits Gellner’s teaching but disputes sufficiency of modernist explanation; neither position is a consensus. Gellner’s provocative primordialist label does not define Smith’s own qualified ethno-symbolic position.

relations.relationship: Links nationalism to modern mobility and mastery of a shared literate culture maintained through political and educational institutions.
relations.evidence_note: Retained primary Gellner reply, with newly inspected central paragraphs on mobility/high culture and contingent continuities. These are his explanatory claims, not a universal outcome or an assertion that cultures lacked any earlier political expression.

relations.relationship: Contests the explanatory necessity of premodern cultural continuity while acknowledging that such continuity sometimes exists.
relations.evidence_note: Direct named Warwick reply to Smith’s opening; both are primary debate statements. Gellner’s provocative primordialist label is not adopted as Smith’s self-definition; Gellner explicitly concedes contingent continuities. No collective nationalism-field arrow is changed.
